title: Incident Overview | Flydubai Flight 1073was a regularly...
text: Flydubai Flight 1073was a regularly scheduled international passenger flight operated byFlydubaifromDubai International Airportin Dubai, United Arab Emirates (UAE), toBen Gurion AirportnearTel Aviv, Israel. On 30 September 2026, while en route, theBoeing 737 MAX 8experienced what Israeli and UAE officials have called an attempted terrorist attack.

title: Incident Overview (Part 2) | According to passenger reports, thefirst...
text: According to passenger reports, thefirst officer, Hamam al-Hammami, attacked and seriously wounded thecaptain,Smit Machchhar, with the cockpitcrash axe. Al-Hammami then sent the plane into a steep descent, in an apparent attempt tohijackand crash it. This caused structural damage to the aircraft'srudderdue tooverspeed. The captain was able to open the cockpit door to let in passengers, who restrained the first officer and stabilized the plane. Other Flydubai pilotsdeadheading on boardthen landed the plane in Tabuk. Al-Hammami was taken into custody after the landing. The incident is under investigation primarily by law enforcement agencies from Israel and the UAE. Images of formeral-QaedaleaderAyman al-Zawahiriand suicide bomberHumam Khalil Abu-Mulal al-Balawiwere found on al-Hammami's social media. He reportedly planned to crash the plane into a Tel Aviv skyscraper, or into Ben Gurion Airport.

title: Aircraft | The aircraft involved in the...
text: The aircraft involved in the incident was aBoeing 737 MAX 8, registered as A6-FKF. The plane entered service with Flydubai on 21 December 2022. At the time of the incident, the aircraft was approximately three years and nine months old.Flydubai is owned by theInvestment Corporation of Dubai.

title: Passengers and crew | The crew included two operating...
text: The crew included two operating pilots: an Indian captain,Smit Machchhar, who was thepilot flying, and Hamam al-Hammami,an Omanifirst officerwho was thepilot monitoring.Machchhar, age 38,trained as a pilot at Mainland Air inDunedin, New Zealand,and flew forSpiceJetfor 11 years before joining Flydubai in 2022.At the time of the incident he had logged about 9,750 hours on the Boeing 737 series, 6,400 of them as pilot-in-command.

title: Passengers and crew (Part 2) | The crew also included twodeadheading...
text: The crew also included twodeadheading pilotsin the passenger cabinin order to operate the return flight back toDubai:one British,and the other European from an unspecified country.

title: Middle Eastern conflict | Due to the ongoingconflict across...
text: Due to the ongoingconflict across the Middle East, several Western airlines reduced flights to Israel, but the airlines of the UAE continued to provide multiple flights each day between Dubai and Tel Aviv.

title: Middle Eastern conflict (Part 2) | On 29 September, the day...
text: On 29 September, the day before Flydubai Flight 1073, Israeli prime ministerBenjamin Netanyahusaid he had received indications that Israel might be attacked ahead of the upcominglegislative electionon 27 October. Political opponents dismissed the statement as "fearmongering".Opposition leaderYair Lapidwas briefed shortly thereafter and denounced Netanyahu's warning and insisted there was no reason to panic.Lapid later stated, "Nothing even remotely resembling the [Flydubai Flight 1073] incident came up in the security briefing."

title: Incident | Flight 1073 departed from Dubai...
text: Flight 1073 departed from Dubai at 7:05a.m.GSTtraveling west to Tel Aviv.The flight was scheduled to be three and one-half hours, and the incident started roughly an hour before its expected arrival.While flying near theSaudi Arabia-Jordan borderat 9:21a.m. GST,the aircraft plunged from an altitude of approximately34,000ft (10,000m)to17,000ft (5,200m)in less than a minute,diving towards the ground at speeds estimated at600 miles per hour (970km/h).The plane briefly rose to21,750ft (6,600m), before descending again to15,000ft (4,600m)and turning back into Saudiairspace.Shortly after the initial dive, the aircraft'stransponderbroadcast squawk code 7700, indicating a general emergency, and shortly thereafter broadcast code 7500, indicating "unlawful interference" or a hijacking.

title: Incident (Part 2) | Based on initial assessments by...
text: Based on initial assessments by authorities and video and eyewitness accounts from passengers, al-Hammami, thefirst officer, stabbed and seriously wounded the captain,Smit Machchhar, using the crash axe kept in the cockpit,in an alleged attempt to gain control of the aircraft and crash it.In a televised interview with Netanyahu, Machchhar said "The co-pilot wanted to pray. A lot of the locals, they do pray, which is not out of the ordinary. While he was praying, out of respect, I was just looking at the front and not at the back - and suddenly after about four, five minutes, there was a big blow to the back of my head."The sound of the struggle alerted Tali Manes, a mother waiting for her daughter to finish using the nearby lavatory.Tali informed her husband, Tzvika Manes, sitting in the front row, and one of the twodeadheadingpilots on board.Meanwhile, Machchhar managed to click the release to open the cockpit door from the inside, which otherwise would have been difficult to penetrate.Tzvika saw Machchhar fall out of the cockpit with the first officer "on top of him, stabbing him" as the plane began to dive.

title: Incident (Part 3) | One of the deadheading pilots...
text: One of the deadheading pilots (identified by the passengers as "James"),Tzvika, and other passengers, including Yaniv Hayun, Shota Musayev, and Asaf Rajuan then attempted to enter the cockpit,which Hayun said was difficult because the captain's body was resting against the door.They then overpowered al-Hammami, who was allegedly attempting to disable or damage the flight controls, and removed him from the cockpit.Hayun stated that he pulled back on theyoketo level the plane, based on the knowledge learned from watching the Canadian documentary seriesMayday.The deadheading pilot "James" then took over,and was later joined by the other deadheading pilot.Al-Hammami was initially restrained withheadphonewires,and reportedly yelled "Kill me, kill me";he was later restrained withcable ties.Musayev, a dentist, treated the captain's injuries.

title: Incident (Part 4) | Upon receiving the hijacking code...
text: Upon receiving the hijacking code and being unable to contact the flight for 30 minutes,theIsraeli Air Forcescrambled fighter jets.Under certain conditions, and with the approval of the Israeli prime minister, Israeli Air Force protocol calls for a rogue flight approaching Israel to be shot out of the sky.The aircraft continued west intoJordanianairspace before turning around and heading back toward Saudi Arabia,at which point the fighter jets were recalled.After an hour flying at its new altitude of15,000ft (4,600m), the plane landed safely atPrince Sultan bin Abdulaziz AirportinTabuk, in northwestern Saudi Arabia at 10:45a.m. GST (9:45a.m.SAST).Photographs taken after the landing showed that most of the aircraft'srudderwas missing; it had likely detached during the rapid descent when the plane exceeded its maximum design speed.

title: Incident (Part 5) | Upon landing, al-Hammami was arrested...
text: Upon landing, al-Hammami was arrested by Saudi authorities.Both injured pilots were taken to nearby hospitals.The captain was in serious condition after sustaining deep cuts to the head and hands;his condition was later reported to be stable.Musayev said that he feared that if the landing had been delayed by even a few more moments, the captain would not have survived.One passenger was also hospitalized, and some passengers required bandages for minor injuries, but most passengers were physically unharmed.

title: Investigation | Al-Hammami is an Omani nationalwho...
text: Al-Hammami is an Omani nationalwho had worked for the airline since February 2026.He was 29 years old at the time of the incident, and was born to an Omani father and Syrian mother.According to Netanyahu, "he was suicidal, that's not a question" and interrogation revealed he had undergoneIslamist radical indoctrination.According to Saudi television stationAl Arabiya, he was radicalized while in Syria.Under its agreement with Israel, Flydubai was obligated to exclude Omani pilots from any of its Israeli operations becauseOman and Israel do not have diplomatic relations.

title: Investigation (Part 2) | In 2024, extremist material had...
text: In 2024, extremist material had been found in al-Hammami's possession while he worked forOman Air.Oman Air suspended him from piloting because he had radical ideological views,assigned him an administrative role, and enrolled him in aderadicalizationprogram,but Oman Air did not share its concerns more broadly.

title: Investigation (Part 3) | On 1 October 2026, al-Hammami...
text: On 1 October 2026, al-Hammami was transferred to the UAE,which launched an investigation into the incident, the motive, the weapon used,and any possible link to terrorism.Israel joined the investigation.ABC Newsreported that Al-Hammami was cooperating with UAE authorities, and indicated he had intended to crash the aircraft in Israel.Law enforcement agencies from Saudi Arabia and the United States are monitoring the investigation.

title: Investigation (Part 4) | On 2 October, images of...
text: On 2 October, images of formeral-QaedaleaderAyman al-Zawahiriandtriple agentsuicide bomberHumam Khalil Abu-Mulal al-Balawiwere discovered on al-Hammami's social media.

title: Investigation (Part 5) | On 4 October, theAustralian Federal...
text: On 4 October, theAustralian Federal Policeconfirmed an investigation by a counterterrorism team to determine whether al-Hammami became radicalized while on a student visa in Australia between 2015 and 2017.Also on 4 October,The Times of Israelreported that al-Hamammi had intended to crash the plane into a Tel Aviv skyscraper or Ben Gurion Airport.

title: Investigation (Part 6) | On 5 October,The Wall Street...
text: On 5 October,The Wall Street Journalreported that Flydubai had performed a criminal-background check on al-Hammami when he was hired, but did not contact Oman to vet his experience, and that he had flown to Israel on multiple occasions.Al-Hammami reportedly told his interrogators that he acted in retaliation for theGaza warand wished to die as amartyr.

title: Aftermath | In an official statement, Flydubai...
text: In an official statement, Flydubai confirmed that an "incident" had occurred during the flight, noting that the plane landed safely in Tabuk and that all passengers were secure.A second statement cited "an altercation" on the flight deck, called the motives unknown, and said on-duty crew travelling on the flight landed the aircraft.

title: Aftermath (Part 2) | Saudi Arabia, which has nodiplomatic...
text: Saudi Arabia, which has nodiplomatic relations with Israel, refused a request to allow Israeli military aircraft to retrieve Israeli passengers from Tabuk;instead, Flydubai sent two replacement aircraft to Tabuk to fly the passengers to Tel Aviv.

title: Aftermath (Part 3) | Netanyahu and Defence MinisterIsrael Katzheld...
text: Netanyahu and Defence MinisterIsrael Katzheld a security consultation, andIsrael Defense Forces(IDF) chief of staffEyal Zamirheld a situational assessment with commander of the Israeli Air ForceOmer Tischlerand other senior military officials.Israeli and UAE officials called it an attempted terrorist attack,and Netanyahu said that it was too early to establish who was behind the attack.Netanyahu and Indian prime ministerNarendra Modiboth praised Captain Machchhar.

title: Aftermath (Part 4) | Netanyahu announced new security measures...
text: Netanyahu announced new security measures in response to the incident.Following Israeli transport ministerMiri Regev's advice, Israel suspended all Flydubai flights to the country for six days.The UAE agreed to Israel's security demands, allowingEl Al,Arkia, andIsrairto resume flights after being restricted byIsraeli security forcesfor the preceding six months over unresolved security concerns stemming from theMiddle Eastern conflict.The three airlines announced that they would resume service to Dubai on 2 October to bring back Israelis remaining there; El Al's landing slot was delayed until 3 October.

title: Aftermath (Part 5) | On the morning of 1...
text: On the morning of 1 October, the captain and first officer were flown from Saudi Arabia to the UAE after they were medically cleared for travel.The captain continued to receive medical treatment in the UAE.The same day, US presidentDonald Trumpthreatened to hit Iran "very hard" if it was behind the thwarted attack, suggesting that the Omani first officer was linked toTehran"based on what I'm hearing," but did not provide further details.

title: Aftermath (Part 6) | On 2 October,Anwar Gargash, Emirati...
text: On 2 October,Anwar Gargash, Emirati senior adviser to UAE presidentMohammed bin Zayed, became the first senior Emirati official to publicly state the incident was an "act of terrorism".

title: Aftermath (Part 7) | On 4 October, theIsraeli governmentsaid...
text: On 4 October, theIsraeli governmentsaid that it does not independently vet foreign pilots,but relies on international airlines confirming that they have vetted the pilots in accordance with international standards.The same day, Netanyahu ordered "a thorough review" of security procedures for international flights to Israel.

title: False flag conspiracy theories | Shortly after the incident, social...
text: Shortly after the incident, social media posts speculating that the incident was an Israeli-plannedfalse flagoperation began circulating online.The Antisemitism Research Center (ARC), an AI-powered social mediamass surveillanceproject of theCombat Antisemitism Movement(CAM), stated that conspiracy theories were being spread as early as 67 minutes after the plane squawked an emergency signal (i.e., while the plane was still in the air), and that it was likely part of a coordinated propaganda campaign against Israel byIranianandRussianstate agencies. CAM issued a report stating that 2,963 of 4,136 social media reports collected in the 12-hour period after the hijacking included false flag conspiracy theories.Oliver Marks, a surveillance analyst at ARC, said "this isn't a narrative that forms in response to an incident... it's part of a script that already exists, sitting ready for use whenever opportunities arise."

title: Analysis | Richard J. Levy of Aviation...
text: Richard J. Levy of Aviation Experts Consulting, a retired airline captain,said that the wounded captain sending an emergency signal and managing to unlock the cockpit door while under attack was remarkable.He also said it was astonishing that the aircraft was flyable after the rudder was ripped off.

title: Analysis (Part 2) | Sally Leivesley, an aviation security...
text: Sally Leivesley, an aviation security expert, estimated that the plane pulled out of its rapid descent with only five seconds to spare before recovery would have been impossible.

title: Analysis (Part 3) | ABC Newscontributor, former fighter pilot,and...
text: ABC Newscontributor, former fighter pilot,and retiredcolonelSteve Ganyard said it was extraordinary that "a passenger who'd done nothing more than watch television shows,... knew how to recover the airplane and pull just hard enough to recover the airplane, but not so hard that it would do damage or destroy the airplane."

title: Alleged Flydubai hijacker likely wanted to target Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, sources say | The alleged hijacker of the...
text: The alleged hijacker of the Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv likely wanted to target Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, the country's main international gateway, according to an Israeli official and an Israeli source familiar with the matter.

title: Alleged Flydubai hijacker likely wanted to target Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, sources say (Part 2) | Hamam al-Hammami,the suspect in the...
text: Hamam al-Hammami,the suspect in the hijacking attempt and co-pilot on board the flight,was stopped by the actionsof the captain and several passengers who restrained him and wrested control of the airplane.

title: Alleged Flydubai hijacker likely wanted to target Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, sources say (Part 3) | The official and the source...
text: The official and the source said Israel is receiving updates from the Emiratis and that the investigation was still in its early stages. There are still questions about the suspect's intentions, they added.

title: Alleged Flydubai hijacker likely wanted to target Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, sources say (Part 4) | It's unclear why al-Hammami allegedly...
text: It's unclear why al-Hammami allegedly attacked the captain,Smit Machchhar,over Saudi airspace if his goal was to target an airport in Israel. When Israel detected an inbound commercial jet signaling a potential hijacking on September 30, authorities there scrambled Israeli fighter jets as a precaution - standard procedure for such an emergency scenario.

title: Alleged Flydubai hijacker likely wanted to target Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, sources say (Part 5) | The United Arab Emirates is...
text: The United Arab Emirates is leading the investigation into the attempted hijacking on board Flydubai's FZ1073 to learn the motives behind the attack and understand how the suspect was able toget through the safeguardsof two countries known for their strict security protocols.

title: Alleged Flydubai hijacker likely wanted to target Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, sources say (Part 6) | Israel's Tax Authority confirmed the...
text: Israel's Tax Authority confirmed the names of all passengers and crew were in the hands of Israeli authorities before the flight had taken off, but it said questions about the vetting of crew members should be referred to the Ministry of Transport. Shin Bet, Israel's internal security agency, also referred CNN to the Ministry of Transport, which it said is "responsible for all security matters concerning foreign airlines."

title: Alleged Flydubai hijacker likely wanted to target Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, sources say (Part 7) | The Ministry of Transport said...
text: The Ministry of Transport said that its procedures do not include checking the names of flight crew members, although those names are submitted to the Israel Tax Authority, which collects them in case of requests by security services.

title: Alleged Flydubai hijacker likely wanted to target Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, sources say (Part 8) | The ministry added that all...
text: The ministry added that all flight crew members are required to have a travel visa to enter the country, and an Omani passport should have been flagged at check-in. But the ministry also said its "procedures do not address the threat from a pilot."

title: Suspect likely acted alone | CNN reported on Sunday that...
text: CNN reported on Sunday that the suspectprobably acted alone, and Israel is so far not aware of a link to any terrorist organization that trained, funded, or organized the attack.

title: Suspect likely acted alone (Part 2) | The attorney general of the...
text: The attorney general of the UAE, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, said the co-pilot on board the flight had attempted to seize control of the plane by attacking his colleague with a crash ax - a piece of equipment required on most aircraft. The attorney general called the attempted hijacking a "terrorist act."

title: Suspect likely acted alone (Part 3) | The suspect, al-Hammami, had been...
text: The suspect, al-Hammami, had been removed from his previous job at Oman's national airline on the track to be a pilot following concerns about his extremist views, sources told CNN earlier. He was moved to a desk job at the company, one of the sources said.

title: Suspect likely acted alone (Part 4) | Flydubai said it couldn't comment...
text: Flydubai said it couldn't comment on the matter while an investigation was underway. CNN has also reached out to Oman Air, the UAE Foreign Ministry and the Dubai government's media office for comment.

title: Suspect likely acted alone (Part 5) | Aviation experts have told CNN...
text: Aviation experts have told CNN that when it comes to vetting pilots, the responsibility lies with local governments, airlines and security services. Experts said pilots' licenses and security passes are handled at the national level, and the rules vary depending on the country.

title: Flydubai co-pilot planned to crash plane into Tel Aviv airport or building, reports say | The co-pilot accused of trying...
text: The co-pilot accused of trying to hijack a flydubai plane planned to crash the aircraft into Tel Aviv's Ben Gurion airport or a tower block in the Israeli city, US and Israeli reports suggest.

title: Flydubai co-pilot planned to crash plane into Tel Aviv airport or building, reports say (Part 2) | The United Arab Emirates' attorney-general...
text: The United Arab Emirates' attorney-general has said the co-pilot attempted to carry out a "terrorist act" on flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv last Wednesday.

title: Flydubai co-pilot planned to crash plane into Tel Aviv airport or building, reports say (Part 3) | He attacked and wounded the...
text: He attacked and wounded the captain with the emergency crash axe kept in the cockpit before being overpowered by passengers. Another crew travelling on the plane was able to land it in Saudi Arabia.

title: Flydubai co-pilot planned to crash plane into Tel Aviv airport or building, reports say (Part 4) | Israel's prime minister has said...
text: Israel's prime minister has said the co-pilot underwent "Islamist radical indoctrination" and the captain, passengers and a second crew prevented "a 9/11 disaster".

title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says | More details about the co-pilot...
text: More details about the co-pilot of the flydubai flight - whom multiple reports have named as Hamam al-Hammami - emerged over the weekend as he continued to be questioned in the UAE, with Israeli representatives being updated.

title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says (Part 2) | Israeli media cited sources with...
text: Israeli media cited sources with knowledge of the probe as saying the co-pilot told investigators that, having attacked Capt Smit Machchhar, he intended to continue flying the plane as normal into Israeli airspace and receive landing clearances from Ben Gurion airport.

title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says (Part 3) | He then planned to crash...
text: He then planned to crash the Boeing 737 MAX - with more than 180 passengers on board - into the airport or into a tower block in central Tel Aviv, in the style of al-Qaeda's 11 September 2001 attacks in the US, according to the reports.

title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says (Part 4) | The co-pilot also reportedly told...
text: The co-pilot also reportedly told investigators that he had intended to hijack and crash a previous flight to Tel Aviv but changed his mind because he knew someone on board.

title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says (Part 5) | UAE Attorney-General Hamad al-Shamsi said...
text: UAE Attorney-General Hamad al-Shamsi said on Saturday that his country's investigations would establish the full circumstances, motives and any links related to the incident, and that the results would be announced upon their conclusion.

title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says (Part 6) | Questions are also being asked...
text: Questions are also being asked about major security lapses, including how the attacker was recruited by flydubai and given clearance to fly a plane filled with Israelis to Tel Aviv.

title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says (Part 7) | Regional officials said the co-pilot...
text: Regional officials said the co-pilot was barred from flying by Oman's national carrier, Oman Air, and moved to an administrative job because of concerns about his extremist views.

title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says (Part 8) | He was later hired by...
text: He was later hired by UAE-based flydubai after undergoing standard security checks that did not examine his background for potential signs of radicalisation, according to the officials.

title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says (Part 9) | Israeli aviation regulations also state...
text: Israeli aviation regulations also state that pilots who are citizens of countries without formal diplomatic relations with Israel, like Oman, are not permitted to operate flights to the country.

title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says (Part 10) | Regional officials told the Associated...
text: Regional officials told the Associated Press on Sunday that Emirati authorities had shared with Israel a list of passengers and crew ahead of flight FZ1073's departure.

title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says (Part 11) | But Transport Minister Miri Regev...
text: But Transport Minister Miri Regev said her ministry was not given passenger and crew lists, and that security oversight for flights operated by foreign airlines fell under the remit of the Shin Bet and the Mossad foreign intelligence agency.

title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says (Part 12) | Israel's Prime Minister, Benjamin Netanyahu,...
text: Israel's Prime Minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has told the head of the National Security Council to review "all security aspects regarding foreign civil aviation to Israel".

title: Incident Overview (Part 3) | I am relieved to confirm...
text: I am relieved to confirm that all 172 passengers and crew on board are safe and being cared for. This includes our Captain, who has now returned to the UAE following medical clearance. We will continue to provide everyone affected with the support they need.

title: Incident Overview (Part 4) | I want to express my...
text: I want to express my deep gratitude to our Captain, the pilots who secured the aircraft and landed it safely, as well as our cabin crew. I extend our sincere gratitude to the passengers on board who assisted our crew during a challenging situation.

title: Incident Overview (Part 5) | On behalf of everyone at...
text: On behalf of everyone at flydubai, I extend my sincere thanks to the authorities in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for their swift and professional response. I also thank the UAE authorities and relevant stakeholders for their support in helping our customers and crew return home.

title: Incident Overview (Part 6) | At the request of the...
text: At the request of the authorities, we have temporarily suspended operations to Tel Aviv until further notice. ​ Our teams are working around the clock to support disrupted passengers and help them reach their final destinations.

title: Incident Overview (Part 7) | I know there are many...
text: I know there are many questions about what happened on board FZ 1073. A full official investigation, led by the relevant authorities and fully supported by flydubai, is underway. It is important that we allow this process to establish the facts.

title: Incident Overview (Part 8) | Following the incident involving flight...
text: Following the incident involving flight FZ 1073 on 30 September, and in coordination with the relevant authorities, flydubai flights to and from Israel will be suspended while the investigation continues.

title: Incident Overview (Part 9) | The safety and wellbeing of...
text: The safety and wellbeing of our passengers, crew and operations remain our highest priority. This temporary suspension will allow the relevant authorities to continue their work and establish all the facts surrounding the incident.

title: Incident Overview (Part 10) | We are fully committed to...
text: We are fully committed to supporting the ongoing investigation and maintaining the highest safety standards across our network. We remain in close coordination with government authorities, regulators and airport stakeholders and will review the suspension as more information becomes available.

title: Incident Overview (Part 11) | An altercation occurred in the...
text: An altercation occurred in the flight deck of flight FZ 1073, operating from Dubai International (DXB) to Ben Gurion International Airport (TLV), on 30 September.

title: Incident Overview (Part 12) | The aircraft was successfully secured...
text: The aircraft was successfully secured by on-duty flydubai crew travelling on the flight, who diverted and landed the aircraft safely at Tabuk Airport (TUU). All passengers and crew are safe and accounted for.

title: Incident Overview (Part 13) | At this early stage, the...
text: At this early stage, the underlying reasons and motives behind this event are unknown and remain subject to a formal investigation. We urge all parties to refrain from premature speculation while authorities gather the facts.

title: Incident Overview (Part 14) | Our immediate priority is to...
text: Our immediate priority is to ensure the ongoing safety, health, and wellbeing of all passengers and crew members involved in this incident and support the official investigation.

title: Incident Overview (Part 15) | flydubai can confirm that flight...
text: flydubai can confirm that flight FZ 1073 operating from Dubai International (DXB) to Ben Gurion International Airport (TLV) on 30 September experienced an incident while en route. The aircraft has landed safely in Tabuk Airport (TUU) and all passengers are safe and accounted for. The safety and wellbeing of our passengers and crew remain our highest priority.

title: Incident Overview (Part 16) | From its home in Dubai,...
text: From its home in Dubai, flydubai has created a network of more than 125 destinations served by a fleet of 98 aircraft. Since commencing operations in June 2009, flydubai has been committed to removing barriers to travel, creating free flows of trade and tourism and enhancing connectivity between different cultures across its ever-expanding network.

title: Incident Overview (Part 17) | An expanding network: Created a...
text: An expanding network: Created a network of more than 125 destinations in 56 countries across Africa, Central Asia, the Caucasus, Central and Southeast Europe, the GCC and the Middle East, South Asia and Southeast Asia.

title: Incident Overview (Part 18) | Serving underserved markets: Opened more...
text: Serving underserved markets: Opened more than 100 new routes that did not previously have direct air links to Dubai or were not served by a UAE national carrier from Dubai.

title: Incident Overview (Part 19) | An efficient single fleet-type: Operates...
text: An efficient single fleet-type: Operates a single fleet-type of 98 Boeing 737 aircraft and includes: 25 Next-Generation Boeing 737-800, 69 Boeing 737 MAX 8 and 04 Boeing 737 MAX 9 aircraft.

title: Incident Overview (Part 21) | An attack by the copilot...
text: An attack by the copilot on the pilot during aFlydubaiflight has raised many questions regarding aviation security, and some of the official versions of the incident have come under scrutiny from online commentators and aviation enthusiasts.

title: Incident Overview (Part 22) | About two and a half...
text: About two and a half hours after Flight FZ1073 departed from Dubai International Airport on Wednesday, it went into a sharp descent before eventually making an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

title: Recommended Stories | Media reports said the copilot...
text: Media reports said the copilot attacked Captain Smit Machchhar. Passengers were able to overpower the copilot, identified by media asHamam al-Hammami, after Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door during the attack, which the prosecutor general of the United Arab Emirates said was carried out with the cockpit's crash axe.

title: Recommended Stories (Part 2) | While investigators continue working to...
text: While investigators continue working to establish a motive for the attack, several questions have arisen about the incident more generally across social media.

title: Why was al-Hammami allowed to fly despite being flagged over security concerns? | On Friday, The Wall Street...
text: On Friday, The Wall Street Journal quoted unnamed sources as saying that Omani authorities previously blocked the suspect from flying in the country due to concerns over his ideological views.

title: Why was al-Hammami allowed to fly despite being flagged over security concerns? (Part 2) | On Saturday, CNN reported, quoting...
text: On Saturday, CNN reported, quoting a regional diplomatic source, that the copilot had also been removed from flight training over similar concerns and was later reassigned to another position.

title: Why was al-Hammami allowed to fly despite being flagged over security concerns? (Part 3) | It added, quoting two sources...
text: It added, quoting two sources familiar with the matter, that the pilot was removed from a job at Oman's national airline last year over concerns about his views.

title: The possibility of a plumber stabilising plane before reserve pilots stepped in | In a video with Netanyahu,...
text: In a video with Netanyahu, who met him at the airport, Hayoun, 50, was asked how he knew what to do at the plane's controls before another pilot took control. He said: "I watch Air Crash Investigation, Mr Prime Minister."

title: The possibility of a plumber stabilising plane before reserve pilots stepped in (Part 2) | "I jumped back, grabbed the...
text: "I jumped back, grabbed the controls and started pulling back the handles" the way he had seen in the Canadian investigation show, in which experts analyse plane crashes.

title: No report of mass injuries despite fall of 5,180 metres | According to the flight-tracking website...
text: According to the flight-tracking website Flightradar24, the Flydubai flight rapidly descended about two and a half hours after takeoff, dropping more than 5,180 metres (17,000ft) in less than two minutes.

title: No report of mass injuries despite fall of 5,180 metres (Part 2) | While the midair drop caused...

title: flydubai passengers could receive $210,000 each | The attempt last Wednesday by...
text: The attempt last Wednesday by the co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv to crash the plane was thwarted, but many of the passengers are still trying to digest what happened to them and to deal with the trauma. We asked aviation law experts what compensation the passengers could be entitled to, and how they can obtain it.According to US network CBS, the evidence so far is that the co-pilot acted alone, and was not associated with a terrorist organization or a state actor.Adv. Shay Ben-Haim, who has represented foreign airlines in Israel for over thirty years, explains that a passenger who was on the flydubai flight could be entitled to compensation of $210,000 (NIS 600,000), the maximum liability, depending on the extent of the damage caused to him or her and the evidence presented."Under section 21 of theMontreal Convention, the liability of an air carrier is limited to 151,880 special drawing rights, which is currently equivalent to $210,000 per passenger," Ben-Haim says."This limited liability is not a fixed compensation sum to which a passenger is entitled in the event of an attack, injury, or death in the course of a flight, but a ceiling, which means that each passenger bears the burden of proving the extent of damage caused to him or her with evidence."Ben-Haim adds that in certain cases an airline may be liable to more than is provided for in the Montreal Convention. "An airline could be liable to pay compensation over and above the limit if the damage to the passenger is greater than that limit and the airline fails to prove that the damage was a result of negligence or a wrongful act by a third party or by the passenger himself."Adv Boaz Regev, an expert on aviation law, points out that these cases have a short proscription period, and a claim must be filed within two years of the date of the incident. He says that the incident, the damage, and the connection between them need to be demonstrated. Proving substantial psychological damage entails an opinion from a psychiatrist, and the company's guilt also needs to be proved.What is the legal basis for a claim? What is the Montreal Convention, and what does it say?"The Montreal Convention, which applies in Israel through the Air Transport Law 1980, is the sole track for suing the airline. It cannot be circumvented via a regular torts lawsuit," Regev explains."The Convention established two tracks: bodily injury caused by an ‘accident' on the plane, a hijack and a terrorist attack being considered ‘accidents'; and damage caused by lateness."Regev relates that in a case in which he represented a couple against Spanish airline Iberia, "the District Court and the Supreme Court ruled unanimously that the Montreal Convention allows for compensation for non-financial damage, such as distress, on the lateness track, even without physical damage."The Supreme Court left open the question whether it would be possible to claim compensation solely for psychological damage on the ‘accident' track, but Israeli precedent going back to the Entebbe episode recognized this under the previous convention, and the consumerist approach in the Iberia Airlines v. Fleischer Peled case supports this. In the US, the approach is narrower."Is it possible to sue a foreign airline, and if so where?"The Montreal Convention applies when two countries (the take-off and destination airports) are parties to the Convention. Flydubai can therefore be sued in the courts in Israel," Ben-Haim explains, and points out that every airline that receives an operating permit from the Israel Civil Aviation Authority must have a representative on whom lawsuits can be served in Israel.Regev adds: "If the ticket was purchased via another company, that company can be sued as well. The Convention allows a lawsuit to be filed in the destination country of the flight, and for bodily injury in the country in which the passenger is resident as well. Israeli passengers can therefore sue Flydubai in the Israeli courts."Can the lawsuit be filed as a class action on behalf of all the passengers, or does each passenger have to sue privately?"It may be possible to file a claim as a class action, but the claimants are liable to have difficulty in proving similar damage, and so to the extent that the damage is different from one passenger to another, it may be worthwhile filing separate lawsuits."In my view, this case is not very suitable for a class action, as the damage caused to each passenger is not necessarily the same, but should an application for recognition as a class action be filed, it cannot be ruled out that it might be approved as such by the court."What is the precedent that matches the facts of the case?The case that has a certain similarity to the Flydubai incident is the Entebbe operation in 1976, in which Air France Flight 139 from Tel Aviv to Paris was hijacked after a stop in Athens, and was forced by the hijackers to deviate from its planned course and to land at Entebbe Airport in Uganda. Almost all the passengers were later rescued from the place in which they were held hostage. Only after several years did they decide to sue Air France for the psychological damage caused to them and for the suffering they had undergone. The suit, however much it may have been justified, was dismissed, because of the short, two-year proscription period, which had passed by the time the lawsuit was filed."I allow myself to assume that had the lawsuit been filed in a court in Israel within two years of the date of the incident, no-one would have doubted that it was not proscribed, and that the right to sue existed," Judge Dov Levin said at the time.Later in his judgment Judge Levin wrote, "There is no obstacle to including hijackings in the definition of the term ‘accident'," and that "From the point of view of judicial policy, it is appropriate to interpret section 17 [of the Warsaw Convention, which the Montreal Convention largely replaced] broadly, such that by virtue of it it will be possible to award compensation for psychological damage alone."Is there any other way of suing over a terror incident?Ad. Regev responds positively. "The Victims of Hostile Actions (Pensions) Law, 1970 applies to Israeli citizens even if they are harmed overseas. It entitles people to medical treatment, rehabilitation, and allowances from the National Insurance Institute, including for psychological disability such as post-traumatic stress disorder. The condition is that the Ministry of Defense recognizes the event as a ‘hostile action.'"For an event overseas, that requires, among other things, that the action was carried out by a hostile state or organization or to promote their aims, or was directed at Israel or at Jews. That determination depends on the findings of the investigation. When the circumstances point towards that with a fair degree of probability, the law assumes that it was a hostile attack. This track does not preclude a claim against an airline, and there is a mechanism for coordination between them."Published by Globes, Israel business news -en.globes.co.il- on October 4, 2026.© Copyright of Globes Publisher Itonut (1983) Ltd., 2026.
